learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected About 99% and locked the annual top-of-atmosphere polar sunlight prediction relative to the equator.
observations.exploration: Selected the equator: beam ground width factor 1.00 and annual sunlight 100%. At 60 north, the equinox noon beam spread over twice the width, extra distance was 3,186 km or 0.002%, and annual sunlight was 57%. At the North Pole, the beam grazed the horizon, extra distance was 6,371 km or 0.004%, and annual sunlight was 41%, with a summer all-day-sun note.
observations.reveal: The reveal corrected the answer to about 40%, gave 41%, and distinguished the negligible distance effect from angle-driven spreading. It explained that low all-day summer sun prevents the annual polar total from being zero.
observations.visual: Inspected the inline dark 1257 by 936 screenshot at 60 north. A fixed-width band of parallel rays touched a longer highlighted ground segment on a circular Earth. The diagram was labelled equinox noon, while a separate readout explicitly said year's sunlight versus equator.
observations.isolation: No-history evaluation preview banner present. Visible trust count ignored.
observations.reference: Own CUA tab 543884163 snapshots and inspected inline screenshot; no screenshot file saved.

prediction.reason: The quantitative options require distinguishing a tiny distance effect from a large angular effect.

interaction.reason: Latitude presets compare beam spreading with distance and annual energy.
interaction.evidence: Equator, 60 north and pole show increasing spread and sharply lower annual totals despite tiny distance fractions.

payoff.reason: The reveal explains both the lower total and why it remains substantial.
payoff.evidence: It contrasts negligible distance with angle and summer daylight.

clarity.reason: Explicit labels separate instantaneous geometry from yearly totals.
clarity.evidence: Equinox noon appears under the diagram and annual sunlight has its own readout.

transfer.reason: The geometric principle is explained but no new application is worked.
transfer.evidence: All comparisons concern the same Earth latitude question.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast audit, phone, zoom/reflow and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: The pole still gets about two fifths of equatorial annual sunlight despite low angles.
surprise.evidence: The polar state reports 41% with months of all-day summer sun.

visualExplanation.reason: The same beam covering more ground makes reduced energy density visible.
visualExplanation.evidence: At 60 north the highlighted ground segment is twice the reference width.

playfulness.reason: Latitude choices allow controlled comparison rather than open experimentation.
playfulness.evidence: Four presets move the highlighted beam location.

practicalValue.reason: It clarifies a common cause of climate differences.
practicalValue.evidence: The reveal rejects distance as the important driver of the polar gap.

depth.reason: It distinguishes distance, angle and seasonal duration.
depth.evidence: The ending explains both the large gap and the nonzero polar annual total.

complexity.reason: The beam analogy is accessible, but comparing equinox geometry with annual integration requires care.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Moderate: separate energy density, distance and duration across seasons.
complexity.conceptualChallenge: Low sunlight angle spreads energy while seasonal daylight partly compensates.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Latitude, equinox and top-of-atmosphere annual totals are introduced.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Moderate: degrees, width factors, distance percentages and yearly ratios.

whyCool: A tiny change in distance accompanies a large energy change because geometry spreads the same sunlight across more ground.
caveat: The diagram shows equinox noon while the readout is annual; the labels distinguish them, but the seasonal integration is not visualized.
missingEvidence: No seasonal animation or fresh latitude was tested.
